**Kiddie-SADS** is a manualized, semi-structured diagnostic interview method used in child and adolescent psychiatry. In the context of the Danish national quality monitoring for ADHD, it is recognized as one of three approved methods—alongside PSE-SCAN and DAWBA—for fulfilling [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]] [^src1] [^src2]. This indicator measures the proportion of diagnostic pathways for children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 where a standardized diagnostic interview or clinical environmental observation is conducted within 120 days of the assessment's start [^src1]. 

The application of Kiddie-SADS is considered crucial for ensuring a standardized and valid assessment of core ADHD symptoms, differential diagnoses, and comorbidities [^src1]. It is formally classified as a [[full-semistructured-interview]] [^src3]. However, national guidelines and quality reports note that while highly valuable, a full semi-structured interview like Kiddie-SADS or PSE is not strictly deemed necessary in every single case [^src3].

The usage of Kiddie-SADS is tracked in the annual quality reports from the ADHD-DATABASE (2023 and 2024) to evaluate diagnostic certainty, geographic equality, and the implementation of national guidelines across Danish regions [^src1] [^src2]. These reports highlight systemic challenges, such as significant regional variations and low national target fulfillment (e.g., 48% in 2023), while also identifying departments like Odense BUP that successfully implement these standardized methods to ensure diagnostic security [^src1].
